Name: Aleax
Goal: Pray
Why this pairing: A hostile minion an angered lawful god sends after you — prayer gone wrong, made flesh
What it is there: A minion a lawful god sends against a hero who has angered it; looks like the hero.

Name: Aligned Cleric
Goal: Worship at an altar
Why this pairing: Tends the co-aligned temple altar where worship and sacrifice happen
What it is there: Tends a temple's altar; donating to it or worshipping there is how a hero deals with the gods.

Name: Hexaghost
Goal: Complete a ritual with multiple steps
Why this pairing: Its six flames light one per turn through a fixed seven-step pattern before Inferno; the wiki calls the fight a race to kill it before turn 9.
What it is there: An Act 1 boss (or a Mind Bloom fight in Act 3): a ring of six ghostly flames.

Name: Satan
Goal: Make a deal with a devil
Why this pairing: Sheol's boss; Devil Rooms trade heart containers for items
What it is there: The boss of Sheol; the fight opens with The Fallen.

Name: Krampus
Goal: Trade health for resources
Why this pairing: The Devil Room's boss — the room where items cost heart containers
What it is there: A mini-boss that can appear in a Devil Room in place of the deals, firing Brimstone lasers. (The Don't Starve note on this row is still there.)
Clones: Revita Kid (Revita): a hero who pays for everything with their own soul, whose level-up would be this goal ('Beat a game while having paid with your own health')

Name: Uriel
Goal: Deal holy damage
Why this pairing: Angel Room mini-boss; fires beams of light in a cross pattern Check: Uriel's goal is fine, but which release added the angels (Wrath of the Lamb or Rebirth) is unconfirmed, so the Game may want to be Rebirth.
What it is there: An angel mini-boss, appearing when an Angel Room's statue is blown up; Gabriel is the other.

Name: Skeleton
Goal: Defeat a skeleton
Why this pairing: Right about the creature, but the goal repeats live ones: the Bony's 'Defeat 5 skeletons' and Ball x Pit's three skeleton goals; its one quirk (losing its head at 1 HP and running) is the live Pacer's 'Defeat a headless enemy'. Worth a no.
What it is there: A Zone 1 monster that moves every second beat; yellow and black skeletons lose their head at 1 HP and run from the last attack.

Name: Zombie
Goal: Defeat a zombie
Why this pairing: Slow, relentless, never stops walking at you
What it is there: A Zone 1 monster that walks every second beat in a straight line and turns around when it hits an obstruction; King Conga's lines are made of them.

Name: Awakened One
Goal: Defeat a boss that feeds on your powers
Why this pairing: Its Curiosity gives it Strength every time you play a Power, and when its HP hits 0 it is reborn, keeping that Strength. (The old row's 'resurrect yourself 3 times' was about the player, not it.)
What it is there: The Act 3 boss, leader of the Cultists: two phases, the second after it 'dies' and awakens.

Name: Necromancer
Goal: Attack a deceased enemy
Why this pairing: Raises a skeleton from a corpse and re-raises it

Name: Ghost
Goal: Defeat an enemy that only comes for you when your back is turned
Why this pairing: The Ghost pursues you every beat but is stationary and can't be attacked unless you have your back turned, so you have to let it close in. The old goal ('Gain an extra life') had nothing to do with it. Mario's Boo made the idea famous; this is the roguelike one.
What it is there: A Zone 1 monster, 1 HP, that moves only while the player faces away from it.

Name: Mummy
Goal: Open a coffin or sarcophagus
Why this pairing: Mummies lie in tombs; opening a coffin or sarcophagus is a thing many games offer (Diablo, Spelunky, Crypt of the NecroDancer). The old goal, burying a body, is possible in almost none.
What it is there: A whole monster class of wrapped undead (kobold mummy up to giant mummy), found in tombs and the Archeologist's quest.

Name: Violet Fungus
Goal: Obtain a mushroom
Why this pairing: A mushroom that fights back; its corpse is the mushroom
What it is there: A stationary fungus that grabs and sticks to the hero.

Name: Slime Creature
Goal: Fight a group of enemies in a corridor, so only one can reach you at a time
Why this pairing: Slime creatures merge into bigger, deadlier ones when they bunch up, so the classic answer is to retreat into a corridor and take them one by one. Corridor fighting is the oldest roguelike tactic and works in any dungeon game. The old goal (double your max health) was unrelated.
What it is there: A jelly that merges with nearby slime creatures into large, very large and enormous versions, each with more HP and damage.

Name: Monster Lord
Goal: Grow in size
Why this pairing: Lords are twice the size of their counterpart, with doubled HP and damage
What it is there: Any of several monsters spawned as a 'lord': twice the size, with doubled HP and damage; they drop a Scroll of Gigantism or 24 gold.

Name: Larry Jr.
Goal: Defeat an enemy made of several segments
Why this pairing: Larry Jr. is a worm of separate segments, each with its own health. The old goal (hit 5 enemies at once) wasn't his.
What it is there: A segmented worm boss of the Basement: 1-4 bodies, 22 HP per segment.

Name: Fat Gremlin
Goal: Defeat 3 gremlins
Why this pairing: Gremlins come as a gang of four drawn from five kinds (Fat, Mad, Shield, Sneaky, Wizard), so three in one fight is the Gremlin Gang. (The old rows gave Fat Gremlin 'Have 5 of the same item', Mad Gremlin 'gets stronger when hit' and Shield Gremlin 'damage equal to your block'; the first two weren't about the monster and the second repeats DCSS's Hydra, so the gremlins are one row now.)
What it is there: Act 1's gremlins: the Fat Gremlin applies Weak, the Mad one gets angrier when hit, the Shield one hands out block.

Name: Spiker
Goal: Defeat an enemy that damages you back
Why this pairing: Spikers keep building Thorns, so every attack on one hurts you back and it gets worse the longer you wait.
What it is there: One of Act 3's Shapes, with the Exploder and the Repulsor.

Name: Writhing Mass
Goal: Face an enemy that changes every time you hit it
Why this pairing: Reactive: it rerolls its intent whenever it's hit; Malleable: it gains block each time too. It is never the same enemy twice.

Name: Byrds
Goal: Attack every enemy on screen at once
Why this pairing: Byrds come three at a time and fly (halving damage) until hit enough to fall; area attacks are the classic answer.
What it is there: An Act 2 bird that flies, pecks in flurries and is stunned when knocked out of the air.

Name: Sentry
Goal: Defeat 3 robots
Why this pairing: Sentries are constructs fought in a row of three as an Act 1 Elite, alternating Bolt (Dazed) and Beam. (The old row's 'do three things in one turn' wasn't about them.)
What it is there: An Act 1 Elite construct, fought three at a time, with Artifact.

Name: Oklob Plant
Goal: Win a fight without moving
Why this pairing: Rooted forever and still lethal
What it is there: A stationary plant that spits acid at range; it never moves.

Name: The Concierge
Goal: Beat a boss without taking damage
Why this pairing: Every Dead Cells boss has an achievement for beating it 'without taking a single hit', and the Concierge's is the first a player can earn: his stab has a long, clear wind-up.
What it is there: The first tier 1 boss, on the Black Bridge: a hulking jailer who stabs, leaps, shouts you away between phases and wraps himself in an Aura of Laceration.
Clones: Acceptance (Revita): two bosses back to back (Enigma, then Acceptance) without a hit, for Acceptance's Memento

Name: Knight Bullet Kin
Goal: Blow up an enemy with an explosive barrel
Why this pairing: Bullet Kin and their armoured knights shoot explosive barrels to catch you in the blast, without checking how close they're standing, and blow themselves up. (The old row's helmet and 'no headgear' aren't in the wiki: they wear full plate, and armour is already NecroDancer's goal.)
What it is there: Bullet Kin in rusty full plate, only in the R&G Dept: fast-firing but with crawling bullets, flipping tables and shooting barrels.
Clones: Truck Hermit Crab (Dave the Diver): a boss no weapon can hurt, beaten by dropping five explosive barrels on it from above

Name: Nymph
Goal: Get naked
Why this pairing: Charms you into handing over worn armour, then teleports away
What it is there: Steals an item, armour included, and teleports away.

Name: Watchman
Goal: Do not kill any innocents
Why this pairing: Peaceful until you swing; killing one is a murder
What it is there: Keeps the peace in Minetown; angers if the hero kills peacefuls or damages the town.

Name: The Manacle
Goal: Win with a negative modifier
Why this pairing: -1 hand size for the blind

Name: The Water
Goal: Win a fight without discarding or rerolling anything
Why this pairing: Fixed against the wiki: The Water starts the round with 0 discards (it doesn't touch consumables). The ask is to win with the hand you're dealt: no discards, no rerolls.

Name: Greed
Goal: Never skip an offered reward
Why this pairing: The boss that takes everything on offer
What it is there: A Deadly Sin mini-boss who turns up in Shops and Secret Rooms.

Name: Super Greed
Goal: Never buy more than 2 things in one shop
Why this pairing: Greed's escalation — a shop-flavoured body for a shop rule
What it is there: Greed's stronger version, in a Shop or Secret Room once Greed has been met.

Name: Providence
Goal: Hurt a shielded boss with damage over time
Why this pairing: He shields himself at 66% and 33% health, and from then on every hit lands for 1, except damage over time (Thallium, the Rusty Knife), which goes through at full strength.
What it is there: The final boss, 'Bulwark of the Weak', on the crashed UES Contact Light: slashes and shockwaves, then two Gilded Wurms, then a shade of himself.

Name: I.D.P.D. Elite
Goal: Get the police on your trail
Why this pairing: The Inter-Dimensional Police Department comes through portals to kill you once you get too powerful; the more portals open, the tougher the troops (Grunts, then Inspectors, then Shielders).
What it is there: The I.D.P.D.'s troops, built as the player's equal with tech instead of mutations. The old goal (kill every enemy you meet) had nothing to do with them; they even leave you alone if you stand still.

Name: Black Pudding
Goal: Defeat 5 of the same kind of enemy
Why this pairing: Pudding farming: the thing players do with a black pudding is make it multiply and kill the copies. The old goal (upgrade a weapon) had nothing to do with it.
What it is there: Divides when hit with an iron weapon, which players exploit ('pudding farming') for endless corpses.

Name: Gronk
Goal: Fight with a weapon in each hand
Why this pairing: Fixed against the wiki: Gronk forges nothing. He is a giant goblin holding a Gronk's Sword in each hand, the fastest ground unit in the game.

Name: Warlock
Goal: Enchant an item 5+ times
Why this pairing: Its darts degrade what you carry; stacking enchantment anyway is the counter

Name: Disenchanter
Goal: Get an item or ability downgraded
Why this pairing: Its touch strips enchantment off what you wield or wear
What it is there: Its touch drains the enchantment from your gear.

Name: Mind Flayer
Goal: Lose an ability permanently and win anyway
Why this pairing: Eats an intrinsic straight out of your head
What it is there: Sucks out the hero's brain: Intelligence loss and amnesia.

Name: Keystone Kops
Goal: Steal from a shop and escape
Why this pairing: Spawn the moment you leave without paying and chase you
What it is there: Swarm out when the hero leaves a shop without paying.

Name: Aurelionite
Goal: Make a boss beatable by activating every beacon around it
Why this pairing: Aurelionite is invincible until every Halcyon Beacon on the Gilded Coast is paid for and lit, and the beacons go out again after a while. (The old row's 'obtain 5 max tier items' wasn't about her; she is a boss, not an enemy.)
What it is there: A golden Stone Titan with horns and a massive sword, the special boss of the Gilded Coast, reached through a Gold Portal from an Altar of Gold.
Clones: Formless Prime (Voidigo): like every boss there, its health bar is locked until you light every beacon on the level, and it hunts you from room to room meanwhile

Name: Golden Monkey
Goal: Acquire a gem or a diamond
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: in Spelunky 2 the Golden Monkey is a friendly character (Kali's gift for a sacrificed Golden Idol, a monkey a Sorceress turned to gold), not an enemy, which the goal-enemy rule asks for. The goal itself is fine.

Name: Glyphid Praetorian
Goal: Hit an armoured enemy in its open mouth
Why this pairing: Praetorians are plated in Heavy Armor that blocks all damage until each plate breaks, but their mouths have no plating, and they open them to spray acid. The old goal ('Mine an ore') had nothing to do with it. Aiming for the weak spot is how half of all action-game bosses fall.
What it is there: A large armoured Glyphid with an acid spray of deceptive range; the abdomen is unarmoured too.

Name: Mimic
Goal: Open 10 locked doors or chests
Why this pairing: A locked chest that turns out to be a monster

Name: Minotaur
Goal: Break down a door
Why this pairing: Kept from the blind pass; the wiki's Monsters article, as read, doesn't list the Minotaur, so its charge couldn't be checked.

Name: Treadnaught
Goal: Defeat a tank
Why this pairing: It's a tank, with four corner turrets, that can only drive in straight lines. (The old row's 'pilot a vehicle' has the player driving, which the fight doesn't; vehicles already have three goals.)
What it is there: A Black Powder Mine boss: a tank driving the room's horizontals and verticals while its corner turrets fire on their own.

Name: Xi Construct
Goal: Step inside an enemy's shield to hit it
Why this pairing: Its Xi Barrier is a golden bubble that stops shots from outside but not from inside, so you walk in and fight it there. (The old row said 'pilot a flying machine', which nothing in the fight involves; it is a boss.)
What it is there: A Survivors of the Void boss of the Construct family: a beam cannon that keeps summoning four Alpha Constructs and throws up a bubble shield below half health.

Name: DM-200
Goal: Repair a vehicle or a machine
Why this pairing: Dwarven machinery still running long after its keepers died

Name: DM-300
Goal: Fix a broken machine
Why this pairing: The broken mining machine boss

Name: The Giant
Goal: Interrupt an attack before it finishes charging
Why this pairing: The Giant charges each fist three times before a special attack, and destroying the charging fist first interrupts it. (The old row filed him as an enemy who destroys a building; he is a boss, and the fight is about his fists.)
What it is there: A tier 2 boss from Rise of the Giant: a colossus in Guardian's Haven, hurt only through the eye that pops out when a fist is destroyed. His skeleton lies in the Prisoners' Quarters until you beat the Hand of the King.

Name: Goblin Leader
Goal: Build a house or a base
Why this pairing: Spawns from a goblin camp you placed — appears because you built something

Name: Strider
Goal: Touch water
Why this pairing: Downpour is waist-deep water and Striders swim it, pits included Check: the goal is a pun on water striders rather than anything this spider does. Probably worth dropping.
What it is there: A variant on the wiki's Spider page; nothing about it involves water.

Name: Dingle
Goal: Enter a sewer
Why this pairing: The sewage boss; Flushmaster already covers flushing Tagged stinky: the live Dross location's goal is 'Defeat a stinky enemy' and no body carries that tag yet.
What it is there: The boss version of the Dips (living poops) in the Basement: fires shots and whistles up more Dips.

Name: Ukko
Goal: Defeat an enemy you heard before you saw
Why this pairing: Ukko is famous for being heard first: the crackle is the warning. Sound cues before a fight are common. The old goal (change the weather) wasn't about it.
What it is there: The Thunder Mage of the Snowy Depths and the Vault: a telltale electric crackling gives it away before it fires its charged thunder projectile.

Name: Slog of the Cloaca
Goal: Defeat an enemy whose attack changes with the ground it stands on
Why this pairing: Slog spews whatever liquid it is undulating on, and each one does something different when it knocks you prone (black ooze can give you glotrot or ironshank, brown sludge rusts your metal, green goo poisons); on dry ground it can't spew at all.
What it is there: A legendary mollusk in the Cloaca of Golgotha, faster in deep liquid. The old row asked you to carry four liquids, which Slog has nothing to do with.

Name: Ylialkemisti
Goal: Drink a mystery liquid
Why this pairing: The high alchemist — unlabelled flasks, unpredictable results
What it is there: The High Alchemist, boss of the Abandoned Alchemy Lab: slow, with deadly projectiles and a field that reflects shots back; drops the Greek spells.

Name: Limatoukka
Goal: Dig an enemy out of solid rock to fight it
Why this pairing: Limatoukka has to be dug out of the rock before it can be fought, which is the whole encounter; it hits far too hard for a Low body. The old goal (be solid, liquid and gas) wasn't about it.
What it is there: The Slime Maggot: a miniboss embedded in dense rock in the Meat Realm, bleeding poison and biting for extreme damage.

Name: Gas Spore
Goal: Defeat an enemy whose death kills another enemy
Why this pairing: A gas spore's whole point is the explosion it leaves behind: kill it next to something else and both die. The old goal (a boss in one turn) was unrelated, and 'explode an enemy' is already the King Bomber's goal.
What it is there: Explodes when killed, hurting everything around it; floats like a floating eye.
Clones: Psy-Linked Gunner (Beneath Oresa): deals 25 damage to every other enemy when it is killed, a gunner rather than a floating bomb

Name: The Time Keeper
Goal: Get hooked and pulled in by an enemy
Why this pairing: Her Hook and Slash throws a hook that drags you to her and roots you for the slash. (The old row's 'beat the clock' is about Dead Cells' timed doors, not her; that idea is the Timed Door object row now. She is a boss, not an enemy.)
What it is there: The first tier 2 boss, in the Clock Room: a ninja who throws shurikens, hooks you in, dashes the length of the room and rains swords. 'It's in this room that the Time K... No, it was in this room that...'

Name: Death
Goal: Reach level 30
Why this pairing: Arrives at the 30-minute mark — the game's hard timer with a scythe

Name: Deep Blues
Goal: Defeat the king of an army of chess pieces
Why this pairing: Deep Blues is an entire chessboard of enemies (pawns that promote, knights that jump, a rook that castles), and the fight ends when the King falls; the King won't attack until the rest are dead and teleports away if hit early. The old goal ('Complete a daily or weekly run') described something else.
What it is there: A boss: a full chess army, named after the chess computer Deep Blue.

Name: Cerberus
Goal: Pet a pet
Why this pairing: The House's three-headed watchdog, and petting him is one of the best-loved things in Hades; in the Temple of Styx you bribe him with a Satyr Sack, his favourite snack.
What it is there: The infernal watchdog guarding the Underworld's exit, companion of Hades and Zagreus.
Clones: Dog (Colt Canyon): a wild dog that can be tamed (a long-unofficial secret), which unlocks it as a playable character

Name: Little Dog
Goal: Feed an animal
Why this pairing: Feeding is how a pet stays yours
What it is there: A common starting pet; feeding it treats keeps it loyal.

Name: Leshy
Goal: Tame an enemy
Why this pairing: Bishops can be recruited into your cult once beaten, and Leshy is the first. Check: 'Defeat an enemy you can then recruit' is also a Pokémon Mystery Dungeon candidate, so one of the two should go.
What it is there: The youngest of the four Bishops of the Old Faith, ruler of Darkwood and the first major boss; after the story, the bishops can be recruited as followers.

Name: Kallamar
Goal: Defeat a boss that keeps running away from you
Why this pairing: Kallamar's fight is a chase: he refuses to stand and face you. The old goal (catch 5 creatures) wasn't his.
What it is there: The second-eldest Bishop, ruler of Anchordeep: the hardest boss in the game, and famously unwilling to face the Lamb.

Name: Medusa
Goal: Turn an enemy to stone
Why this pairing: Medusa is a unique boss in NetHack, not a rank-and-file monster, and petrification is what she does. The old goal (have an enemy kill 3 others) wasn't hers, and 'reflect a projectile' is already a live goal (Host), so the counter-trick is out. NetHack's bosses are now three: Medusa, Vlad, the Wizard.
What it is there: The unique boss of Medusa's Island, whose gaze turns whoever meets it to stone.

Name: Dar Blademaster
Goal: Train an ally to be stronger
Why this pairing: Brogue allies grow: they learn abilities from the corpses of what they kill (a centipede's weakness, a mystic's shield), and a Wand of Empowerment makes one stronger and smarter. The blademaster is the ally that needs least looking after, blinking out of trouble on his own.
What it is there: A dar swordsman, found in packs from depth 10, who blinks towards his enemies and sometimes carries an item; often found captive and freed as an ally.

Name: Dracula
Goal: Encounter a character from another series
Why this pairing: Dracula comes from Castlevania, with Richter, Alucard, Maria and Death, in the Return to Castlevania DLC: a whole other series' cast walking into this one.
What it is there: A tier 3 boss in the Master's Keep who teleports between attacks; beaten, his arena transforms and he returns in his Final Form.

Name: Kolmisilma
Goal: Wake a boss by taking the treasure it guards
Why this pairing: The fight starts the moment you take the Sampo, a trigger many games share. It is the final boss, so High rather than Low, and the old goal (play a game in another language) was a joke about the Finnish names rather than about it.
What it is there: Kolmisilmä (Three-Eye), the final boss in The Laboratory: curled up beside the Sampo until you grab it, then the arena floods with lava.

Name: Hush
Goal: Reach a hidden area within a time limit
Why this pairing: Hush is only ever met by reaching the Blue Womb fast enough; racing a clock to a secret place is a goal any game with timed secrets can host. The old goal (a new achievement) wasn't about Hush.
What it is there: The boss of the Blue Womb (???), reachable only if you get there within a time limit.

Name: Delirium
Goal: Defeat a boss that turns into other bosses
Why this pairing: Delirium's whole fight is borrowing other bosses' forms. The old goal (10 achievements in a run) wasn't about it.
What it is there: The boss of The Void (Afterbirth+), which teleports and turns into other bosses mid-fight.

Name: Voidling
Goal: Enter a void
Why this pairing: You reach it by going down into the void itself, through the Void Fields and the Void Locus to the Planetarium.
What it is there: The alternate final boss (Survivors of the Void), fought around the ring of the Planetarium in the depths of the void, gaining an attack each phase.

Name: Ultra Greed
Goal: Beat a boss in a game's alternate mode
Why this pairing: Ultra Greed is Greed Mode's final boss; most roguelikes have an alternate mode with its own ending. The old goal (unlock a character) wasn't about it.
What it is there: The final boss of Greed Mode, the wave-based alternate mode.

Name: Johannes
Goal: Defeat the character you played at the start of the game
Why this pairing: The tutorial has you play Johannes, the knight who murders the king for the Fountain of Youth; the final boss is Johannes again, grey as a statue, in the same hall. (The old row's 'play a character that looks like you' wasn't in the wiki.)
What it is there: The Traitor, first phase of the final boss: he chases you with attacks and spells drawn from the player's own classes.

Name: Hand of the King
Goal: Hit a shielded enemy from behind
Why this pairing: His shield turns projectiles from the front and drops only while he attacks, so you get round him or wait for his swing. (The old row's 'beat a game you would rate 8 or higher' wasn't about him, or checkable.)
What it is there: The usual final boss, in the Throne Room: the king's armoured right hand, with a front shield, a charging attack he doubles in his third phase, and resistance to freeze and stun.
Clones: Shield Giant (The Rogue Prince of Persia): a Hun behemoth that can only be hit from behind, and grunts in confusion when you roll past its bash

Name: The Fallen
Goal: Defeat a boss that only appears because of a deal you made
Why this pairing: The Fallen comes for you after a devil deal; that's the only thing about it no other body covers. Check: its other trait, splitting in two, is already a live goal (Spike Slime), and the old goal (a push-up per lost run) had nothing to do with it. Possibly worth dropping.
What it is there: A boss that only appears once you have entered a Devil Room; splits into two at half health.

Name: Amalaric Sniper
Goal: Reach maximum crit chance
Why this pairing: One aimed shot from off-screen for a huge chunk

Name: Shotgrub
Goal: Defeat an enemy with a shotgun
Why this pairing: A Shotgun Kin variant: each spread of shells bursts into waving bullets when it hits a wall, which makes it Bullet Hell's priority target.
What it is there: A dangerous Shotgun Kin from Bullet Hell that walks at you firing three spreads at a time.

Name: Cockatrice
Goal: Use an improvised weapon
Why this pairing: Wield the corpse with gloves and petrify what you touch
What it is there: Its touch petrifies; wielding its corpse with gloves turns enemies to stone, the most famous improvised weapon in roguelikes.

Name: Blobulin
Goal: Defeat 4 slimes
Why this pairing: A Blobulon splits into two Blobuloids and each of those into two Blobulins: four slimes from one. (The old row's 'defeat an enemy without violence' and the Devolver aren't on its page; splitting itself is already Spike Slime's live goal, so this counts them.)
What it is there: The smallest Blobulonian: quick, leaves a trail of harmless goop, and dies on touching you.

Name: Violet Vessel
Goal: Make the number 100000 appear
Why this pairing: A finisher blind whose requirement puts six figures on screen

Name: The Lamb
Goal: Defeat a boss that keeps fighting after its body dies
Why this pairing: The Lamb's second phase is its detached head. The old goal (beat a boss on 1 Health) wasn't about it.
What it is there: The boss of the Dark Room; its head carries on fighting after its body falls.

Name: Goo
Goal: Go from 1 health to full health
Why this pairing: Regenerates in the water it sits in

Name: Mega Satan
Goal: Open a door that needs a special key
Why this pairing: Getting to Mega Satan at all means assembling a key, and keys are the one resource here with nothing to spend them on. The old goal (halve your Max Health) wasn't about it.
What it is there: Waits behind the Golden Gate in the Chest and Dark Room, which only opens with both Key Pieces (or the Dad's Key).

Name: Hecate
Goal: Get hexed or cursed
Why this pairing: The Witch of the Crossroads fights with hexes

Name: Chub
Goal: Make an enemy swallow a bomb
Why this pairing: Feeding Chub a bomb is the Chub fight. The old goal ('Puke') wasn't.
What it is there: A worm boss of the Caves that charges you and eats any bomb in its path, stunning itself.

Name: Mom
Goal: Defeat a boss whose whole body you never see
Why this pairing: Mom is fought as a foot, a hand and an eye. 'Defeat your parent' only works in a few games; a boss you never see whole works in many.
What it is there: The first final boss: you only ever see her foot stomping down and her hands and eyes in the doors.

Name: Blue Baby
Goal: Defeat a boss that is a copy of you
Why this pairing: ??? is Isaac himself, dead; mirror matches and doppelganger bosses are a common fight. The old goal (make someone cry) wasn't.
What it is there: ??? (Blue Baby), the boss of the Chest: a dead Isaac.
Clones: Corrupted Void Hunters (Soulstone Survivors): end-of-Titan-Hunt bosses that are corrupted versions of the playable heroes

Name: Mithrix
Goal: Escape a level before it collapses
Why this pairing: Beating Mithrix isn't the end: you then have to get off the moon before the timer runs out, which is what beating the game means. (The old row's 'destroy a planet or a moon' doesn't happen.)
What it is there: The final boss, at the apex of Commencement, the moon of Petrichor V: Providence's banished brother, a cyclopean god who steals your items in his last phase.
Clones: Bandit Boss (Colt Canyon): the final boss of the canyon, after which you still have to fight your way back home through the B-levels, with no collapse timer

Name: Heket
Goal: Defeat a boss while you are starving or out of food
Why this pairing: Heket is the Bishop of hunger ('he of havoc, he of blight; she of hunger, they of might'). The old goal (defeat a green creature) was wrong: she's red. Pairs with the Hungry curse candidate.
What it is there: The second-youngest Bishop, ruler of Anura: a red toad, 'she of hunger' in the bishops' litany, who hops onto the Lamb.

Name: Book of Stabbing
Goal: Defeat a living book
Why this pairing: It's a book that stabs you, and its stabs leave Wounds. Living books turn up in plenty of dungeons (Gungeon's Bookllets, Mewgenics' Grimoire). (The old row was 'Read a book'.)
What it is there: An Act 2 Elite whose multi-stab grows by one each time.

Name: Bullet Kin
Goal: Flip a table
Why this pairing: Bullet Kin walk to tables and flip them for cover, and so can you: table-flipping is one of the Gungeon's own verbs. (The old row's 'skip the tutorial' was about where you first meet them, not what they do.)
What it is there: The commonest member of the Cult of the Gundead: walks at you, fires single bullets, flips tables and shoots barrels.

Name: Witch Doctor
Goal: Sacrifice a creature you defeated
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: the goal is wrong. Witch Doctors curse you through a voodoo skull effigy; sacrifice belongs to Kali's altars. A fix ('get cursed by an enemy') would sit on the live Hexer ability and the Accursed candidate, so the row waits for the owner.

Name: Vampire
Goal: Drink blood
Why this pairing: The Kapala drinks blood; the vampire is where it comes from
What it is there: Also in Dwarf Fortress, where vampires arrive with migrants and hide among the dwarves until someone is found drained of blood: 'Unmask an enemy disguised as one of your own' is the alternative goal from there (https://dwarffortresswiki.org/index.php/Vampire).

Name: Olmec
Goal: Defeat an enemy you cannot damage
Why this pairing: Indestructible — mattock and bombs do nothing

Name: Angry Shopkeeper
Goal: Anger a shopkeeper and survive the floor
Why this pairing: Shoot one and every shopkeeper in the run hunts you

Name: Qilin
Goal: Ride an animal
Why this pairing: A rideable mount, not a vehicle

Name: The Collector
Goal: Fill your inventory to the last slot
Why this pairing: Ambushes when 13+ inventory slots are full — summoned by how you play
What it is there: A wandering Eldritch miniboss that may appear when the inventory is at least 79% full, summoning the heads of dead heroes.

Name: The Shambler
Goal: Play a whole level with no light
Why this pairing: Ambushes at torch level 0
What it is there: An Eldritch miniboss that lurks at 0 torchlight (or comes from its altar), dropping ancestral trinkets.

Name: Swine Prince
Goal: Beat a boss by killing its helper first
Why this pairing: Wilbur buffs him; kill the small one and the fight collapses
What it is there: The Warrens' boss, with Wilbur beside it; striking Wilbur first changes the fight.

Name: Madman
Goal: Survive an enemy that never attacks you directly
Why this pairing: Deals only stress, never damage
What it is there: A deranged human whose Doomsay hits the whole party with stress rather than damage.

Name: The Countess
Goal: Beat a boss while diseased or cursed
Why this pairing: Crimson Court's finale, where the curse is the fight
What it is there: The final boss of the Courtyard (The Crimson Court DLC): a vampiress and the source of the Crimson Curse.

Name: Bone Courtier
Goal: Defeat the enemy at the back of a group first
Why this pairing: Bone Courtier always stands at the back, and taking out the back rank first is how players beat it. The old goal (stop a boss summoning) didn't fit: it isn't a boss and doesn't summon, and Madman already covers stress attacks. It's an early Ruins enemy, so 1-Low.
What it is there: An Unholy enemy of the Ruins that always stands at the back of its party and deals stress with its Tempting Goblet.

Name: The Fanatic
Goal: Keep an ally alive for a whole floor
Why this pairing: He burns your heroes at the stake — the threat, not the escortee
What it is there: A wandering boss who hunts heroes carrying the Crimson Curse and puts one on his pyre.

Name: Thing From The Stars
Goal: Encounter something from space
Why this pairing: The Color of Madness mini-boss
What it is there: An Eldritch miniboss from The Color of Madness DLC: a shard of alien malignity, many turns per round.

Name: Seraph
Goal: Win a fight where the enemy sets an extra rule
Why this pairing: Every Seraph fight adds a rule of its own: the Chaste halves your buffs and debuffs every turn, the Diligent eats the first spell you play each turn, the Temperant Saps your units, the Patient weakens your front line.
What it is there: The Great Traitor, Monster Train's final boss in Ring 8, who puts a Lightwings on the train every turn.

Name: Lightwing
Goal: Protect something for a whole fight
Why this pairing: Seraph puts one on the train every turn of the final fight, and like everything aboard it climbs toward the Pyre, the thing the whole game asks you to protect.
What it is there: A Winged enemy summoned by Seraph, also part of the Pyrewings and Winged Horde fights.

Name: Avowed Gladiator
Goal: Fight on two fronts at once
Why this pairing: The highest-health non-boss enemy in the game, on the rings where two floors are fought at once

Name: Ragewing Assassin
Goal: Defeat an enemy that ignores your front line
Why this pairing: A back-line enemy with Sweep — it never fights the thing you put in front

Name: Kecleon
Game: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red and Blue Rescue Team
Goal: Defeat a shopkeeper
Why this pairing: Rob the shop and the floor fills with double-speed Kecleon

Name: Groudon
Game: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red and Blue Rescue Team
Goal: Defeat an enemy with ten times your health
Why this pairing: 1600+ HP in Magma Cavern

Name: Zapdos
Game: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red and Blue Rescue Team
Goal: Defeat an enemy you can then recruit
Why this pairing: Beat it, then it can join you

Name: Rayquaza
Game: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red and Blue Rescue Team
Goal: Beat a final boss on your first attempt
Why this pairing: Sky Tower's wall, and the run's ending

Name: Primal Dialga
Game: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky
Goal: Defeat a boss that controls time
Why this pairing: The Explorers finale

Name: Zombie Master
Goal: Watch an enemy upgrade another enemy
Why this pairing: Turns a pack of ordinary zombies into spitters and shockers

Name: Shocker Zombie
Goal: Defeat an enemy that shocks you
Why this pairing: The zapper line's evolution

Name: Boomer
Goal: Get covered in something
Why this pairing: Bursts and coats you in bile

Name: Zombie Hulk
Goal: Defeat an enemy that knocks you through a wall
Why this pairing: Made from the strongest humans

Name: Mi-go
Goal: Permanently change your own body
Why this pairing: Lab and temple surgeons — the game's body horror

Name: Skeletal Juggernaut
Goal: Survive until the enemies get stronger
Why this pairing: A tank-sized late-evolution zombie: enormous health, enormous armour, and it only exists because time passed

Name: Chicken Walker
Goal: Defeat a walking machine
Why this pairing: Military hardware still walking its patrol

Name: Behemoth
Goal: Defeat an enemy that takes up four spaces
Why this pairing: Behemoths occupy four tiles instead of one — the footprint goal

Name: Watcher
Goal: Clear a floor without being spotted
Why this pairing: Unarmed; exists only to report you

Name: Programmer
Goal: Watch an enemy turn your ally against you
Why this pairing: Corrupts other robots with EM weaponry, yours included

Name: Hunter
Goal: Be hunted across floors
Why this pairing: Works in pairs to track you down

Name: Swarmer
Goal: Be surrounded on every side
Why this pairing: Small flying bots that overwhelm in groups

Name: Grunt
Goal: Defeat an enemy that outguns you
Why this pairing: The basic front-line combat robot

Name: Operator
Goal: Hack or override a machine
Why this pairing: The robot that works the terminals
Clones: Max (Cobalt Core): a hacker hero whose level-up would be this same goal ('Beat a game while having hacked a machine')

Name: Hauler
Goal: Win using only equipment taken from enemies
Why this pairing: Carries salvage around the complex

Name: Recycler
Goal: Get some scrap
Why this pairing: Collects what is left of the dead

Name: Xucat'
Goal: Carry four curses at once
Why this pairing: Four curses is the cap before the fifth and final one lands

Name: Xak'olchir
Goal: Pay for something with your own blood
Why this pairing: Blood offerings are one of the three ways corruption fills

Name: Champion of Death
Goal: Defeat an enemy while cursed
Why this pairing: Killing a champion is one of only two ways to lift a curse

Name: Dreadful Offspring
Goal: Clear a room where every kill spawns more
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: the goal is wrong. Dreadful Offspring are petrified babies on gliding stone platforms that teleport near you and shoot lightning; kills don't spawn more of them. 'Teleports next to you' repeats Blink Batty (Dungeons of Dredmor), so the row waits for a better goal or a no.

Name: Headless Guardian
Goal: Defeat something with no head
Why this pairing: Checked: the wiki holds (a headless hammer warrior with a floating mask), but the goal repeats the live Pacer ('Defeat a headless enemy').

Name: The Wicked Twins
Goal: Defeat two bosses in one fight
Why this pairing: One encounter, two champions
Clones: Meg & Byte (Beat Blast): a two-part boss, mines and a charging head, where the survivor changes its attack once its partner falls

Name: Infernal Jaguars
Goal: Defeat a big cat
Why this pairing: The Jaguar temple's namesake

Name: Malok paal
Goal: Defeat something stitched from other creatures
Why this pairing: Checked: the Flesh Monstrosity is made of flesh and stone, with a broken stone mask, not stitched together from other creatures; the goal is a loose fit.

Name: Kashio
Goal: Resolve an encounter without fighting
Why this pairing: A Spark Baron you can argue down instead of killing
Clones: Titan Ape (Renowned Explorers: International Society): any of its encounters can be won with friendly or devious talk instead of blows, each changing the enemy's mood

Name: Fellemo
Goal: Turn an enemy into an ally
Why this pairing: Negotiation is a full parallel combat system here

Name: Plocka
Goal: Make an enemy flee or surrender
Why this pairing: Break resolve rather than health

Name: Jake Smuggler
Goal: Complete a side quest or bounty
Why this pairing: The Jakes run the jobs board

Name: Arint
Goal: Meet an enemy that remembers a past run
Why this pairing: Griftlands tracks who you wronged

Name: Weirdling Beast
Goal: Defeat an enemy that heals to full
Why this pairing: Heals to full in a few turns, and does it often

Name: Ukruk the Fierce
Goal: Survive a fight you were meant to lose
Why this pairing: A scripted ambush you are not supposed to win

Name: Bill the Stone Troll
Goal: Unlock a permanent upgrade
Why this pairing: Drops the Transmogrification Chest, which unlocks for all future characters

Name: Grand Corruptor
Goal: Survive a room that hurts you every turn
Why this pairing: Drags you to the Fearscape, which damages you and heals him

Name: Rak'Shor Cultist
Goal: Face an enemy that copies you
Why this pairing: Spawns a shade with your appearance, stats and talents
Clones: Sato the Stagemaster (Shogun Showdown): a boss whose attacks are tiles copied from your own

Name: The Lich
Goal: Defeat a boss you summoned yourself
Why this pairing: Chapter I's boss, brought by the tiles you placed

Name: Harpy
Goal: Change the map to make an enemy appear
Why this pairing: Spawns after you create a mountain peak

Name: Chest
Goal: Defeat a chest that fights back
Why this pairing: Spawns at the start of each loop on a battlefield

Name: Blood Clot
Goal: Defeat an enemy made of blood
Why this pairing: Spawns every 4 days on a blood path

Name: Frost Jailer
Goal: Free something frozen or trapped
Why this pairing: Companions are freed from ice blocks; the Jailer is what puts them there
Clones: Crystal Prisoner (Realm of the Mad God): a prisoner sealed in a self-healing crystal who talks you into breaking him out, then fights you

Name: Truffle
Goal: Defeat a mushroom
Why this pairing: One of the game's named bosses

Name: Eye of the Storm
Goal: Win a fight using only status effects
Why this pairing: The final fight, decided by stacked statuses

Name: Bamboozle
Goal: Win a fight without knowing what the enemy does
Why this pairing: The Act 1 boss, named for the trick it plays, and it splits into Bam and Boozle when it dies

Name: Krunker
Goal: Defeat an enemy that destroys your items
Why this pairing: The Act 2 boss, and a Clunker — the junk that clogs up what you brought

Name: Warden
Goal: Defeat the enemy protecting the others
Why this pairing: Mind-links nearby enemies and hands them damage reduction
What it is there: A Glyphid that never attacks: its spore emitter gives nearby Glyphids half damage taken and regeneration, and a lone Warden screeches Grunts up out of the ground around it.
Clones: Buffer (Brotato): a weak alien that runs from you and buffs every other enemy's health, damage and speed

Name: Bulk Detonator
Goal: Survive an explosion that fills the screen
Why this pairing: Goes off big enough to take the room
What it is there: An Exploder that lived long enough to grow to tremendous size, one of the biggest creatures in the game; it explodes when it dies.

Name: Oppressor
Goal: Defeat an enemy you cannot hurt from the front
Why this pairing: Armoured at the front, soft behind
What it is there: A mutated Praetorian in black armour over every inch of its body except a small green abdomen on its back; slow, and it rushes into melee.

Name: Stingtail
Goal: Get grabbed and escape
Why this pairing: Grabs and drags you out of position
What it is there: A Glyphid whose long tail ends in a five-pronged claw: it grabs its target and drags it into melee range.

Name: Web Spitter
Goal: Get stuck in place and break out
Why this pairing: Webs the ground under you
What it is there: A ranged Glyphid that hangs from walls and ceilings and spits webs that slow its target.

Name: Gorilla
Goal: Defeat a beast in melee
Why this pairing: No weapons, only Primal Lunge
What it is there: An NPC and playable character: Gorillas fight with their fists and Primal Lunge, and are found caged in science labs (freeing one unlocks the Gorilla), in zoos, and in the Park's caves.

Name: Werewolf
Goal: Witness an enemy transform
Why this pairing: Turns when the conditions are right
What it is there: Looks like an Office Drone (all attributes 1) until it turns; as an NPC it only appears hidden, in the Vampire's Big Quest or the Many Werewolves mutator. Killing a Ghost unlocks it.

Name: Cop
Goal: Bribe an officer of the law
Why this pairing: Cops attack anyone they catch breaking the law, and the way past them is to pay: a bribe gives you Above the Law, and all the floor's Cops ignore your crimes. Bribing 3 Cops unlocks the Cop. The old goal ('without killing anyone') was the Doctor's pacifism, not the Cop's.
What it is there: An NPC and playable character patrolling Slums 2-3, Industrial and Downtown, with a baton or a pistol; Cops grow more numerous floor by floor.

Name: The First Hero
Goal: Defeat another game's protagonist
Why this pairing: Skul inverts the usual story: you are the Demon King's skeleton and the heroes are the enemy, and the First Hero, the Sword of Carleon, is the hero you came to slay.
What it is there: The main antagonist and final boss in the Holy Sanctuary, over three phases (sword, light swords and illusions, then his fists).

Name: Elder Ent: Yggdrasil
Goal: Defeat a tree
Why this pairing: A massive, ancient Ent, the living embodiment of the Forest of Harmony, with branches you stand on as platforms.
What it is there: The first stage boss, in the Forest of Harmony; it was filed as an enemy.

Name: Distorted Goddess: Chimera
Goal: Defeat the failed experiment of a mad scientist
Why this pairing: A failed lab experiment meant to be the vessel for the Goddess Leonia's second coming; it introduces itself by devouring the Black Lab chief mid-monologue.
What it is there: The Black Lab's stage boss: two lion heads, snakes on its back, a wing, faces on its shoulders. Its old goal (a creature made of several) repeated Curse of the Dead Gods' stitched creature, which was there first.

Name: Alexander
Goal: Defeat an emperor
Why this pairing: Emperor of Carleon: Alexander, the kingdom's ruler, fought in the Dark Mirror.
What it is there: The Dark Mirror's boss; the wiki lists him on its Bosses page with no page of his own yet.

Name: The Angler
Goal: Defeat an enemy that steals from you mid-fight
Why this pairing: Hooks your last-played card every other turn

Name: The Trapper
Goal: Trade a monster drop for something better
Why this pairing: Turns your dead cards into pelts, which the Trader buys back as creatures

Name: The Prospector
Goal: Turn something you own into currency
Why this pairing: Second phase turns your played cards into gold

Name: Grimora
Goal: Leave a record of a character who died
Why this pairing: The death scrybe; death cards persist into later runs

Name: P03
Goal: Catch the game changing its own rules
Why this pairing: Takes the game over from the inside

Name: The Unfinished Boss
Goal: Defeat an unfinished enemy
Why this pairing: An Uberbot P03 never completed

Name: Ogre
Goal: Free a caged enemy and fight beside it
Why this pairing: Captives are shackled or caged in the early dungeon and fight beside you once freed; the ogre is the classic early one, with high health and huge hits. (Wiki: Cage, and the Ogre page's 'As an ally'.)
What it is there: One of the first big threats: high health, heavy armour and an enormous club, but off balance after every swing, missing its next turn.

Name: Bloat
Goal: Defeat an enemy that bursts into gas when it dies
Why this pairing: Pop it next to you and a cloud of caustic gas fills the room; burn it and the gas never comes. (The old row named a 'paralytic bloat', which the wiki doesn't have: its bloats are caustic, pit and explosive. 'Lose a turn to paralysis' also repeated Angband's 'held in place' candidate, so both changed.)
What it is there: A common, flitting, flying gasbag that drifts into you and bursts, releasing a concentrated cloud of caustic gas; fire kills it without the gas.

Name: Phantom
Goal: Fight something you cannot see
Why this pairing: Phantoms are permanently invisible; you find them by telepathy, by the gap they leave in a gas cloud, or by bumping into them.
What it is there: A fast, flitting, flying undead from depth 16 that is always invisible and hits hard.

Name: Goblin Conjurer
Goal: Defeat a summoner and watch its summons vanish
Why this pairing: The conjurer hides behind swarms of spectral blades, and they all disappear when it dies; reaching it is the fight. (The old row gave it 'let a summon land the killing blow', which is about YOUR summons; that goal moved to the Spectral Blade.)
What it is there: A goblin caster that summons packs of 3-5 spectral blades, usually travelling with other goblins and jackals.

Name: Warden of Yendor
Goal: Escape an enemy that can't be harmed
Why this pairing: Every attack on the Warden fails; all you can do is outpace him, strand him across deep water or lava, or wall him in with sanctuary runes. (The old row said it guards what lies past the required depth; the wiki has it hunting you after you take the Amulet. 'Go deeper' is close to Angband's 'deepest floor' candidate anyway.)
What it is there: An immortal presence that stalks you through the dungeon once you take the Amulet of Yendor, slow but immune to everything.

Name: Fenrir
Goal: Defeat an enemy that hides and lays traps
Why this pairing: Fenrir hides in tall grass and plants invisible bear traps; the goal is his whole fight. He is a miniboss in Mewgenics and the game already ships ten Mewgenics bosses, so he is an ordinary body here.
What it is there: A Hunter-like cat miniboss in The Alley: stays in Tall Grass, plants invisible Beartraps, shoves anyone who hits it.

Name: Boris
Goal: Pop something swollen
Why this pairing: A swollen blob-cat; popping something bloated is the nearest thing a player does in any game. Check: Mewgenics already supplies ten live bosses, so this one may be one too many; it could be an ordinary body instead. (Dungeon Crawl's Boris is a different monster.)
What it is there: The Sewers' boss: a grotesquely bloated Blob-Cat who tramples toward whatever last damaged him, four times a round.

Name: Bob
Goal: Build a vehicle and leave in it
Why this pairing: The last thing you kill once the boat is built and you set sail

Name: Woodman
Goal: Trade with a creature that only fights if you attack it
Why this pairing: Fixed against the wiki: Woodmen are neutral traders in the Trader Camps, swapping items for coins, and stay passive unless attacked or a Chief's Chest is opened. Nothing about trees.

Name: Wyvern
Goal: Defeat a flying beast
Why this pairing: Night-spawning boss

Name: Chief
Goal: Defeat a leader
Why this pairing: One of the six bosses between you and the boat

Name: Skeleton King
Goal: Defeat a crowned undead
Why this pairing: A stage boss with a crown on
What it is there: The final boss of The BONExYARD, king of the skeletons whose rank and file are already live goals here.

Name: Sabertooth
Goal: Defeat an extinct animal
Why this pairing: A stage boss
What it is there: The final boss of The GORYxGRASSLANDS: a sabre-toothed cat.

Name: Lord of Owls
Goal: Defeat a bird
Why this pairing: A stage boss
What it is there: The final boss of The HEAVENLYxGATES.

Name: Shroom Swarm
Goal: Defeat a mushroom colony
Why this pairing: A stage boss made of many bodies
What it is there: The final boss of The FUNGALxFOREST, a mass of mushroom bodies.

Name: Old King
Goal: Defeat a king
Why this pairing: The previous Lead Lord, pushed off his throne and retreated into the Abbey: a dethroned king, and a hard one. (He has no crown to take, so the old row's second half is gone; it was filed as an enemy.)
What it is there: The Abbey of the True Gun's secret boss, a fiercer version of the Bullet King, and a reference to Old King Doran from Demon's Souls.

Name: Kill Pillars
Goal: Defeat four enemies that share one fight
Why this pairing: Four statues possessed by demons, each with its own health bar, moving and jumping as one group.
What it is there: A boss of the Hollow: four pillars that spin bullets through the arena and jump at you together.
Clones: Pentaract (Realm of the Mad God): five towers linked into a pentagram, each dropping loot once all five fall

Name: High Priest
Goal: Defeat a priest
Why this pairing: The Hollow's priest of the Cult of the Gundead, firing homing skulls and darkening the room.
What it is there: A boss of the Hollow that drifts and dashes, rings itself with bullets and homing skulls, and fades into darkness.

Name: Mine Flayer
Goal: Defeat a boss inside a mine
Why this pairing: It lives in the Black Powder Mine and throws claymore mines that chase you; it also hides among bells, and only the right one brings it back.
What it is there: The Black Powder Mine's boss: rings and streams of bullets, walking claymores, and a disappearing act among bells.

Name: King Conga
Goal: Defeat a line of enemies that all follow the one in front
Why this pairing: King Conga sits on a throne that can't be hit, guarded by two conga lines of eight Zombies: the yellow head follows you and every Zombie behind follows the one ahead, and when a head dies the next one takes over. Breaking up the lines is the fight. (The old goal, 'Wear a crown', was about his look, not his fight.)
What it is there: A Zone 1 boss, a gorilla king on a throne; only the Dagger of Phasing hits him while his lines stand.

Name: The Necrodancer
Goal: Do not pause the game
Why this pairing: The game that never stops moving to the beat
What it is there: The final boss, fought as Cadence and Dorian together: pairs of floor switches must be pressed at once to bomb his stage, then he summons minibosses in time with the music.

Name: Coral Riff
Goal: Defeat a musician
Why this pairing: A boss made of instruments
What it is there: A boss in a water-filled arena: an Octoboss whose tentacles are instruments (drums, horns) that surface around you to the beat.

Name: Death Metal
Goal: Defeat an armoured enemy
Why this pairing: A boss in metal armour with a speaker in its chest, three phases deep
What it is there: A boss with 9 health and 4 phases ('Ah, welcome!'): in the first it carries a shield and can only be hit from the sides or behind; later it summons skeletons and throws fireballs.

Name: The Guardian
Goal: Make an enemy change form
Why this pairing: Mode Shift: deal it enough damage and it flips into Defensive Mode, Sharp Hide out, then back again.
What it is there: An Act 1 boss (or a Mind Bloom fight), a great construct with 240 HP. It was filed as an enemy.

Name: Giant Head
Goal: Defeat an enemy that punishes you for being slow
Why this pairing: It counts down for four turns, then uses It Is Time every turn after, harder each time; the longer the fight, the worse it gets.
What it is there: An Act 3 Elite, a huge stone head with 500 HP.

Name: Nemesis
Goal: Defeat an enemy that is untouchable every other turn
Why this pairing: Intangible reduces every hit to 1 damage, and Nemesis gains it every other turn: you have to time your damage. (The old row said it halves damage, which it doesn't.)
What it is there: An Act 3 Elite ghost with a scythe that also burns you.

Name: Dogma
Goal: Break a screen
Why this pairing: A boss who climbs out of the television
What it is there: The first boss of Home (Repentance), attached to a television that has to be destroyed.

Name: Gurdy
Goal: Defeat a boss that never moves
Why this pairing: Gurdy sits still for the whole fight. 'An enemy made of other enemies' didn't describe her.
What it is there: A stationary blob boss of the Caves that never moves.

Name: Monstro
Goal: Defeat an enemy that jumps on you
Why this pairing: The first boss most players ever meet
What it is there: A Basement boss that hops toward you and jumps off-screen to land on you.

Name: The Beast
Goal: Reach an ending most players never see
Why this pairing: Repentance's true finale
What it is there: The final boss of Repentance (Ending 22), and of The Binding of Isaac as a whole.

Name: Bone Hydra
Goal: Defeat an enemy with more than one head
Why this pairing: The Lernaean Bone Hydra, Asphodel's boss: a skeletal hydra that grows extra heads as the fight goes on.
What it is there: The boss of Asphodel, nicknamed Lernie. It was filed as an enemy.

Name: The Furies
Goal: Meet the same boss with a different face
Why this pairing: Tartarus's boss is Megaera at first, then her sisters Alecto or Tisiphone take her place on later runs: the same fight with a different Fury.
What it is there: The three sisters of vengeance, the first boss of every run (Megaera is live already). They were filed as an enemy.

Name: Charybdis
Goal: Get swallowed
Why this pairing: A mouth in the sea

Name: Wizard of Yendor
Goal: Defeat a boss that keeps coming back
Why this pairing: Killed, and then he is back
What it is there: The final antagonist, who keeps coming back after being killed and harasses the hero all the way up.

Name: Scavenger
Goal: Defeat an enemy that uses the same items you do
Why this pairing: 'Tasting your own Medicine': it fights with the planet's items, the ones you pick up yourself (a Disposable Missile Launcher, a Brilliant Behemoth, an Ukulele), and heals with a Mysterious Vial.
What it is there: A late-game pack-rat boss, the only one that can appear on any stage, once the difficulty meter is about three-quarters full.

Name: Magma Worm
Goal: Defeat an enemy that burrows
Why this pairing: 'Ancient Lava Swimmer': it surfaces under you, turns, and dives again, and a patch of flame marks where it will come up.
What it is there: A segmented boss whose only attack is surfacing and submerging; it can drop the Burning Witness.

Name: Imp Overlord
Goal: Defeat something from another dimension
Why this pairing: 'Lord of the Red Plane': it manifests out of empty space, and its imps teleport about through red portals.
What it is there: A boss with fire from the sky and a fast lunge; it drops the Imp Overlord's Tentacle.

Name: Parent
Goal: Defeat an enemy that's hunting you for defeating its child
Why this pairing: The field notes: 'mad with grief and rage... their only aim to crush the butcher of their offspring.' The Child is already in the game.
What it is there: A big, slow ground monster that slams the ground into great cracks. The old row had it grabbing and throwing you, which it doesn't do.

Name: The Wall
Goal: Beat an encounter with double the requirement
Why this pairing: An extra-large blind

Name: The Eye
Goal: Do not use the same attack twice
Why this pairing: No repeat hand types this blind

Name: The Ox
Goal: Lose all your currency at once
Why this pairing: Fixed against the wiki: playing your most played hand this run sets your money to $0. It takes your money; you don't spend it.
Clones: Dramatist (Dice & Fold): takes all your Gold Coins if left standing for 6 turns

Name: Mother
Goal: Defeat an enemy that fills the screen
Why this pairing: Kept from the blind pass, but the wiki can't confirm it: Mother's page gives stats only (+750 health a wave, 100% knockback resistance, speed 250) and no behaviour.
What it is there: An elite, drawn from a zone's elite pool. It is not a wave-20 boss, as the old row said: those are the Predator and the Invoker.

Name: Monk
Goal: Get in close to an enemy that keeps its distance
Why this pairing: The Monk lays 15 Slasher Eggs, then hangs back: it alternates between firing 5 projectiles a second and holding a fixed distance from you while it spawns Tentacles. Closing that distance is the fight. The old goal ('never stops moving') was wrong.
What it is there: An elite: lays 15 Slasher Eggs, then alternates between firing 5 projectiles a second and holding a fixed distance while spawning Tentacles.

Name: Cain
Goal: Defeat a sibling
Why this pairing: Cain is the true final boss and king of Genesis; to reach him you walk past portraits of every heir you've played. The sibling is the biblical Cain's (Abel), which the wiki's page doesn't spell out, so check it in game.
What it is there: The true final boss, in Castle Hamson, behind three broken stained-glass windows.

Name: Estuary Lamech
Goal: Hit two targets without touching the ground
Why this pairing: His door opens only if you spin-kick both red lanterns outside without landing, which needs the Air Dash. (The old row's 'beat the first boss with no upgrades' is the opposite of what reaching him takes.)
What it is there: The first boss, in Citadel Agartha: spear dashes across the arena, spirals of blue fireballs from a staff.
Clones: Combos (Downwell): kill 8 or more enemies in a row before landing and the combo pays gems, a charge and at 25 a point of health

Name: Byarrrith and Halpharrr
Goal: Defeat two enemies that share a health bar
Why this pairing: The second boss is a pair, the Void Beasts of Axis Mundi. That they share one health bar is from memory; the wiki's page doesn't say, so check in game. (Curse of the Dead Gods' 'two bosses in one fight' is the looser version.)
What it is there: The Void Beasts of Axis Mundi, Byarrrith and Halpharrr, the second boss fight.

Name: Xeroc
Goal: Be fooled by something disguised as loot
Why this pairing: Imitates an item until you touch it

Name: Aquator
Goal: Have your armour ruined and keep going
Why this pairing: Rusts armour on contact

Name: Praxis
Goal: Defeat someone who sends others to fight you
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: the final boss in Netherra; on doom mode, holding the Architect's power, he stays in one arena and summons copies of the minibosses (Guzzle, Phalanx, Herald, Scrapper) between his phases.

Name: Plague Bringer
Goal: Win while poisoned
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: a mini-boss of Scoggfirth by name only, with no page; nothing there says it poisons, so the goal can't be confirmed.

Name: The Architect
Goal: Defeat a boss that builds its own arena
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: it has no page for the Architect as a boss. The DLC's final fight is Arch Praxis, in the Architect Realm, with power stolen from the Architect; the row's boss may be misnamed.

Name: Prickwood
Goal: Defeat the first boss of a run
Why this pairing: The first boss the game gives you
Clones: Phrike (Returnal): the first boss as the famous wall of a hard game, asked for on the first attempt rather than at all

Name: Bee Queen
Goal: Defeat a bee or a wasp
Why this pairing: Drops honey balls into the claw machine so everything they touch comes up in one sticky clump

Name: Daemon Master
Goal: Defeat the second to last boss of a run
Why this pairing: Always the penultimate boss — the rest are randomised

Name: Strong Daemon Master
Goal: Defeat a final boss on the highest difficulty
Why this pairing: Always the last boss

Name: Grip
Goal: Defeat a named enemy
Why this pairing: One of Farmer Maggot's dogs, and the first unique most runs ever meet

Name: Wormtongue
Goal: Live through being slowed or held in place
Why this pairing: Saruman's agent opens by slowing you and filling the floor with traps

Name: Boldor
Goal: Defeat the king of the feeblest creatures in the game
Why this pairing: King of the Yeeks, whose subjects are the weakest thing in the dungeon

Name: Sauron
Goal: Defeat the boss standing between you and the last one
Why this pairing: He dies on level 99 or the stairs to Morgoth never appear

Name: Morgoth
Goal: Reach the deepest floor of the game
Why this pairing: Waits on dungeon level 100, which is the bottom of Angband

Name: Kranach
Goal: Clear an optional area the run did not require
Why this pairing: A raider lord in a side quest nothing forces you to take

Name: Keethrax
Goal: Defeat an enemy that curses you when it hits you
Why this pairing: The evil druid of the first quest corrupts by touch

Name: Cat Lord
Goal: Do not harm any animals
Why this pairing: He arrives stronger and angrier for every cat the run has killed

Name: Emperor Lich
Goal: Defeat an enemy that raises the dead against you
Why this pairing: Summons meat shields by the screenful and paralyses on touch

Name: Diggle
Goal: Defeat an enemy guarding its young
Why this pairing: The early floors' bird, found standing over its eggs

Name: Blink Batty
Goal: Defeat an enemy that teleports
Why this pairing: A batty that blinks away the moment you swing at it

Name: Lord Dredmor
Goal: Beat the boss the game is named after
Why this pairing: The whole descent is aimed at him and nothing else

Name: Champion
Goal: Defeat an elite version of an ordinary enemy
Why this pairing: Champions are rolled-up variants of the normal roster

Name: Mamel
Goal: Defeat the weakest enemy in the game
Why this pairing: The first and feeblest monster a Shiren run meets

Name: Gitan Mamel
Goal: Take a fortune off a single enemy
Why this pairing: Drops 2,000 gitan, and moves at double speed so it is hard to collect

Name: Pacorepkin
Goal: Witness an enemy move through solid wall
Why this pairing: Pacorepkins travel through walls

Name: Zoltan
Goal: Put up a shield that stops a hit before it lands
Why this pairing: A Zoltan shield keeps a hit — and a boarding party — off the hull entirely

Name: Mantis Boarder
Goal: Repel an enemy that reaches your own side
Why this pairing: Mantis crews teleport aboard and fight you in your own rooms

Name: Rebel Flagship
Goal: Defeat the final boss of the game
Why this pairing: The Last Stand's three-phase flagship, and the only way a run is won

Name: Psion
Goal: Defeat the enemy that is making the others stronger
Why this pairing: Harmless itself; every other Vek loses its buff the moment it dies

Name: Scarab
Goal: Defeat an enemy that outranges you
Why this pairing: Lobs artillery from five tiles away

Name: Spider Leader
Goal: Destroy an egg before it hatches
Why this pairing: An island boss whose whole threat is the eggs it leaves behind

Name: Titan
Goal: Defeat an enemy that came to attack your home
Why this pairing: A surface megabeast that paths to your fort once it is rich enough to notice
What it is there: A procedurally generated megabeast of the surface, attracted by a fortress's wealth and population, that paths straight to it.

Name: Forgotten Beast
Goal: Meet a monster the game invented for this run
Why this pairing: Procedurally generated in the caverns, and no two are ever the same
What it is there: The underground equivalent of titans: a procedurally generated horror woken by digging too deep.

Name: Bronze Colossus
Goal: Defeat an enemy made of metal
Why this pairing: A bronze statue that has to be worn down rather than hurt; it feels no pain
What it is there: A megabeast in the form of a gigantic bronze humanoid; killed, it leaves a masterwork bronze statue of itself.

Name: Slime
Goal: Poison an enemy
Why this pairing: Its element is Poison and it carries Slime Balls and Toxic Ooze, so a slime is usually the first poison a run meets; the goal turns that round.
What it is there: A low-level enemy that only ever says 'SLORP'. Dislikes broccoli.

Name: Snowman
Goal: Defeat an enemy made of ice or snow
Why this pairing: A buff snowman who came into the dungeon looking for the Fireman, throwing Snowballs that freeze your dice.
What it is there: One of the game's Super enemies; fire and burn equipment is the wiki's advice against him.

Name: Lady Luck
Goal: Win a fight decided by a lucky roll
Why this pairing: The goddess of the gameshow, and the dungeon is dice: the prize she offers is a ruse, and every contestant finally confronts her in the Backstage.
What it is there: The host of Dicey Dungeons and its endgame boss, after every contestant's Bonus Round.

Name: Stumpy Stump
Goal: Defeat an enemy sheltering behind a fallen one's body
Why this pairing: A dead Stump leaves a corpse that can't move or attack but blocks non-piercing shots at whatever stands behind it, so the fight is getting round your own kills. (The old row's 'an enemy that is a plant' sits too close to Skul's 'Defeat a tree'.)
What it is there: A weak Forest tree-stump (200 health, 2 damage) whose boards are packed with bombs and dense pegs.

Name: Thesaurosus
Goal: Meet an enemy whose name is a pun
Why this pairing: A thesaurus-saurus, and Peglin names nearly everything this way (Knight Knight, Slenderlin, Pigment of Imagination, Wand of Skulltimate Greed).
What it is there: The Mines' boss: a stationary dinosaur with 12,000 health whose fire breath pulls your orbs towards a board exit, gaining strength each time one falls in.

Name: Jack of Dust
Goal: Defeat a bandit or a thief
Why this pairing: The Dust suit is human thieves, and the Jack is their elite

Name: King of Scales
Goal: Defeat a lizard or a reptile
Why this pairing: Scales is the lizardman suit; the King is its heaviest card

Name: The Dealer
Goal: Beat the game's own narrator
Why this pairing: He deals the cards all game and is the thirteenth and last boss

Name: Caveman
Goal: Defeat an enemy that charges straight at you
Why this pairing: Runs at you and does nothing else, which is the whole of its plan

Name: Selt
Goal: Jump over an attack
Why this pairing: Selt's rock waves and her closing charge are both dodged by jumping over them, and the jump is UnderMine's own dodge. (The old row said only her tail takes damage; the wiki gives her no weak spot, so 'hit one specific spot' moved to Ponzu, whose crystal is one.)
What it is there: Queen of Sand, the Goldmine's last boss and the cause of its earthquakes: a giant sandworm that lays eggs that hatch into Larvae, sends rock waves while chasing her tail, then burrows and charges.

Name: Seer
Goal: Defeat a boss that leaves fire wherever it walks
Why this pairing: Seer's footprints set you alight, and so does touching her. (The old row's 'beat a boss without healing' repeats a live goal, 'Beat a game without purposefully healing', a size up.)
What it is there: World's Heart, the final boss of the Golden Core: her footprints and her touch ignite, she spits bouncing orbs and meteors, and hides behind a red cloud that a bomb in her face cancels.

Name: Snake
Goal: Defeat a snake
Why this pairing: Fixed against the wiki: nothing ties the snake to the first room. 'Any game featuring a whip-toting, fedora-sporting treasure hunter also stipulates the ophidiophobic hero's worst fear': the Mines' basic snake, now a plain Bounty.

Name: Bones
Goal: Defeat an enemy that another enemy summoned
Why this pairing: Bones are what other monsters summon: the Grave, the Imp, the Wisp and the Chest all have a 'Bone Ritual' side, and the Lich summons them at health breakpoints.
What it is there: A tiny 4-HP skeleton with 3-4 damage on every side; weak alone, deadly as a swarm, and when one dies it hits the monsters above and below it for 1.

Name: Demon
Goal: Defeat a demon
Why this pairing: The Demon is what Hexia, the hardest final boss, summons; players say it can end a run on its own. The wiki has no page for it, so this rests on player comments: check it in game.
What it is there: A monster summoned by Hexia in her final-boss fight (from player discussion; no wiki page).

Name: Shielder
Goal: Strip a shield off an enemy
Why this pairing: Casts shields that eat one instance of damage for an ally

Name: Grappler
Goal: Defeat an enemy that drags you into melee
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: it has no Grappler page, and its enemy table gives only lore ('a formidable foe, the grappler's mysterious origins add to its fearsome reputation'), so dragging you into melee can't be confirmed there.

Name: The Shogun
Goal: Beat a boss that has more than one phase
Why this pairing: The run's target, and he has a second phase

Name: Tick
Goal: Defeat an enemy before it reaches you
Why this pairing: Tiny, arrives in groups, and the whole threat is it getting to the dome

Name: Driller
Goal: Repair something an enemy has broken
Why this pairing: Big and slow, carrying a drill that chews sustained damage into the dome

Name: Barbarian
Game: Legend of Keepers: Career of a Dungeon Manager
Goal: Defeat a hero
Why this pairing: In a game where you are the dungeon, the heroes are the monsters

Name: Priestess
Game: Legend of Keepers: Career of a Dungeon Manager
Goal: Defeat an enemy that heals the others
Why this pairing: The healer in the party raiding your dungeon
Clones: Korlok Tyrant-Weed (Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor): a mini-boss behind spitting sprouts that grows healing pods, so you clear what keeps it alive first; Proteron (Returnal): never attacks at all, and heals every enemy in the room at once through green beams, announced by a pulse as you enter

Name: Owl
Goal: Reach a secret or alternate ending
Why this pairing: The final boss of the Dark Ending, which is not the ending you get by default

Name: Polar Bear
Goal: Defeat a bear
Why this pairing: From the Frozen Heart's roster
What it is there: A beast with 170 HP: 'Rarely seen outside of the arctic wastes and frozen core, polar bears will fight anyone willing to test their mettle.'

Name: Farseer
Goal: See what a room holds before you enter it
Why this pairing: Kept from the blind pass, but the wiki can't confirm it: the Enemies table gives the Farseer 800 HP, the Chosen Cultist's power, a revive into a new phase on defeat, and the line 'He corrupts'. Nothing about seeing ahead beyond the name.
What it is there: A boss with 800 HP that revives and changes phases when defeated.

Name: Wolf
Goal: Defeat a wolf
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: 34 pages, and no Wolf or enemy list beyond a stub, so the body can't be confirmed there.

Name: Houndmaster
Goal: Defeat an enemy that fights alongside an animal
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: no Houndmaster page and a stub enemy list; a search finds nothing.

Name: Former Human
Goal: Defeat someone who used to be on your side
Why this pairing: The colony's own crew, turned; the first thing the game shows you

Name: Turret
Goal: Defeat an enemy that cannot move
Why this pairing: CalSec's bolted-down gun, which shoots and never follows

Name: Prismancer
Goal: Use three different elements in one fight
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: it has pages for spells and only three monsters (the Tormentors), and none for a Prismancer, so neither the enemy nor its elements can be confirmed there.

Name: Archer
Goal: Beat a ranged enemy by standing next to it
Why this pairing: Range 5 and cannot attack an adjacent tile at all

Name: Wizard
Goal: Use an enemy as cover
Why this pairing: Its fire beam will not fire through another demon

Name: Elite Kappa
Goal: Defeat a creature that lives in water
Why this pairing: A kappa is a river spirit, and it fights like one

Name: Abyssal Serpent
Goal: Defeat a giant serpent
Why this pairing: An act boss, and long enough to need the room

Name: Pawn
Goal: Watch a weak enemy turn into a strong one
Why this pairing: Reaches the far side and is promoted into a knight, a rook, a bishop or a queen

Name: Rook
Goal: Defeat an enemy that can only move in straight lines
Why this pairing: It moves and attacks orthogonally and has never done anything else

Name: White King
Goal: Defeat a boss that grows when it is cornered
Why this pairing: Checked against the wiki: nothing says the White King grows when cornered; he is the chess king you hunt across 12 floors, guarded by his pieces. A chess-flavoured fix ('checkmate a king') would repeat the Deep Blues candidates, so the row waits for the owner.

Name: The Butcher
Goal: Meet an enemy that speaks to you
Why this pairing: "Ah, fresh meat!" — greeting you from a room strewn with the townsfolk he butchered
What it is there: A unique overlord with a cleaver in a room of corpses on level 2, who greets you with 'Ah... Fresh meat!'

Name: King Leoric
Goal: Defeat an enemy that heals off the damage it deals
Why this pairing: Diablo's Skeleton King under his own name, since Ball x Pit's crowned one already has the sheet's Skeleton King; he heals for everything he takes off you
What it is there: The Skeleton King, in his tomb off level 3: raises skeletons as they fall, and every point of damage he deals heals him (100% life steal).

Name: Chaos Cyclops
Goal: Defeat a one-eyed enemy
Why this pairing: A chaos-tier body from the Chaos Trials, where every enemy has a chaos variant

Name: Marching Ghost
Goal: Defeat an enemy that moves in formation with others
Why this pairing: The Forgotten Viaduct's ghosts arrive in step and stay in step

Name: Possessed Effigy
Goal: Watch a statue come to life
Why this pairing: An effigy that stops being scenery

Name: The Archivist, King of Old
Goal: Break something a boss is standing on
Why this pairing: Its throne has to come down before the boss itself can be hurt

Name: Treeguard
Goal: Make peace with an enemy you provoked
Why this pairing: It wakes because you cut down its trees, and planting pine cones nearby settles it
What it is there: A walking tree that can rise when an Evergreen is chopped; hostile to the woodcutter, pacified by planting new trees nearby.

Name: Deerclops
Goal: Meet an enemy that only comes out in one season
Why this pairing: Winter only, and it walks through your camp on the way to you
What it is there: A one-eyed giant active only in Winter, which wrecks camps and drains Sanity.

Name: Sloth
Goal: Win a fight with the worst unit you have
Why this pairing: Tier 1, does nothing at all, and is beloved for it

Name: Gelatinous Cube
Goal: Defeat an enemy that engulfs what it touches
Why this pairing: The dungeon's slow-moving cube, straight off the tabletop

Name: Drakee
Goal: Take an item off an enemy that was carrying it
Why this pairing: Monsters here spawn holding an item and drop it when they die

Name: Baezl'bub
Goal: Carry a trophy from the last boss back to where you started
Why this pairing: Kill the arch-daemon on level 25, then carry his heart all the way back to the surface

Name: Grid Bug
Goal: Defeat an enemy with your very first attack
Why this pairing: The first monster most NetHack players ever kill, usually in one swing; a 1-Low body for the bug tag.
What it is there: The weakest monster in the game; it can't move or attack diagonally.

Name: Soldier Ant
Goal: Defeat an enemy that is faster than you
Why this pairing: Famous for being fast and deadly: one of the top causes of death in NetHack. Every game has a fast enemy.
What it is there: A fast, poisonous ant, among the most common early-game killers (#3 on NAO's death list).

Name: Quantum Mechanic
Goal: Get teleported against your will
Why this pairing: Its one attack teleports you; being moved somewhere you didn't choose happens in lots of roguelikes (traps, enemies, portals). 'Defeat an enemy that teleports' is a different goal (Dungeons of Dredmor candidate).
What it is there: A humanoid whose claw teleports its target at random.

Name: Unicorn
Goal: Give a gift to an enemy
Why this pairing: Throwing gems to a unicorn is NetHack's most famous peaceful interaction (it pays in Luck). A gift to an enemy is a Regent-style 'make a friend' moment any game with trading or feeding can host.
What it is there: Three alignments of unicorn; throw it a gem and it may pay you in Luck, kill a co-aligned one and lose Luck.

Name: Vlad the Impaler
Goal: Climb to the top of a tower
Why this pairing: Vlad waits at the top of his own tower; climbing to the top of something is a natural Discovery. No live body carries the vampire tag yet (Spelunky 2's Vampire is the other candidate), and the Whip and Bloody Tear (goal: defeat a vampire) and Antonio's level-up have been waiting for.
What it is there: A unique vampire lord who guards the Candelabrum of Invocation at the top of Vlad's Tower.

Name: Sigmund
Goal: Defeat an enemy far above your level
Why this pairing: Sigmund is the early unique that ends runs: he turns up on the second floor with a scythe and spells meant for a much later one. Beating something out of its depth is a goal every roguelike offers. ('Defeat a named enemy' is already an Angband candidate.)
What it is there: Sigmund the Dreaded, one of the earliest and deadliest uniques (D:2-6), with a scythe, a robe and confusion and invisibility spells.

Name: Hydra
Goal: Defeat an enemy that gets stronger each time you hit it
Why this pairing: Cut a hydra's neck with a slashing weapon and it grows another head (another attack). The live roster has a splitter but nothing that grows from being hit.
